chunks: To you have come signs from your Lord, (and the light of understanding). So any one who sees (and understands) does so for himself, and any one who turns blind shall suffer the consequences alone. (Say:) "I am not a guardian over you (to make you understand)."

key_terms.بَصَائِرُ: Plural of baseerah; clear signs, proofs, or lights of understanding from God

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'basa'ir' in Surah Al-An'am and how does it relate to individual responsibility?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the term 'basa'ir' (plural of basira) is often interpreted not merely as general signs but specifically as the clear proofs of the Imams and the Ahl al-Bayt, who serve as the living manifestations of divine guidance. This verse underscores the principle of individual accountability (mas'uliyya), where the Prophet's role is limited to conveying the message, leaving the ultimate judgment of perception versus blindness to the individual's own spiritual vision. Consequently, the burden of guidance rests on the recipient's capacity to 'see' the truth, highlighting the intrinsic link between divine clarity and human free will.
